en: Sutta Nipāta 2.3 Hirisutta One who crosses over by means of moral shame,
feeling a sense of loathing [for evil].
One who says "I am yours," yet does not take up his own noble deeds—
one should recognize him by thinking, "He is not mine."
He who utters pleasant words to his friends that are not consistent with his actions—
he is not a friend who is always vigilant,
who suspects discord, and looks only for a flaw.
And he upon whose breast one rests like a son—
he indeed is a friend who cannot be alienated by others.
Such a person is a ground for the arising of joy.
The bringing of praise is happiness;
one who bears the human yoke develops the fruit as its benefit.
Having drunk the flavor of solitude and the flavor of tranquility,
one becomes free from distress and free from evil.
They drink the flavor of the joy of the Dhamma.
This is the third discourse on moral shame.
